It provides the exact Upload API and reuses NewFile, whereas B changes the required option type and adds explicitly prohibited association machinery.","reasons":["A implements `Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption)` exactly; B instead uses `...UploadFileOption`, breaking the mandated API and existing `FilesOption` behavior.","A reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content)` as required. B expands the helper with `NewForm` solely to support out-of-contract association fields.","B adds numerous `WithUpload*` association options despite the explicit prohibition on adding association fields.","Both validate empty filenames and nil readers and produce buffered, replayable multipart bodies, but B has the stronger streamed-content retry test using a non-seekable `io.MultiReader`. Neither visibly tests source-reader failure propagation as required by the contract."],"risks_a":["`Upload` duplicates `Add` request construction and response decoding instead of routing the encoded body through `FilesService.Add`, violating a central maintainability requirement.","The broad `RawClient.Do` seekable-body retry and ownership changes are outside the requested scope and alter existing body-closing and Content-Length semantics.","The Upload retry test uses a replayable `strings.Reader`, so it does not specifically prove buffering makes streamed/non-seekable source content retryable."],"risks_b":["The required public method signature is wrong because it accepts `UploadFileOption` rather than `FilesOption`.","It adds prohibited association fields, a parallel option system, and duplicate multipart-form machinery.","Like A, it bypasses `FilesService.Add` and duplicates request/response behavior instead of keeping it centralized and unchanged for options and errors in the required way, while also modifying unrelated retry machinery."]}
